- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0 to +0.3), model tends to overestimate — adjust downward by 2–4% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.3), model often overreacts — cap forecast increase at +3% above recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days shows significant lag — adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% per day of lag to align with true trend.
- If true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving average, model often misses downward trend — add 2–5% downward bias for next 7 days if sentiment is negative.
